title: Ship state persistence across restarts
description: Ship position, regime, hull, shields, cargo, and livery persist across server restarts; on shard spawn the sim loads the exact last saved state (no teleporting to spawn points).
acceptanceCriteria: Shard flush: every 30 s and on graceful shutdown, the shard writes each ship's {pos, vel, quat, regime, hull, shields, livery, onPad} to ships table (single transaction, upsert)
Shard spawn: loads all non-docked ships of the system into sim entities with their saved state; docked ships load at dock coords
Crash test: start server, move a ship 500 u from dock, kill -9 the process, restart, join the system — ship is within 1 u of its last position (tolerance = 1 tick of movement)
Destruction persistence: a destroyed ship persists as wreck until ttl; after ttl it is gone on next load (no orphan rows: cleanup on load deletes expired wrecks)
Concurrency: flush while a player is flying does not block the tick for more than 1 frame (measured in the flush test, sqlite writes are small)
npm run test green including the crash-restart integration test (spawns a real child server process)

steps.details: shard/persist.ts: flushShips(shard) transaction: upsert ships by (player_id) with state fields; called on a 30 s interval + on SIGTERM/SIGINT (graceful shutdown hook in server main).
loadShips(systemId): select ships where system_id = ? and state != 'destroyed' or (wreck and not expired); build sim entities. Expired wrecks deleted in the same transaction.

Test boots the real server on a random port + temp DB file (TASK-68 env), claims a callsign, ws joins, sends inputs for ~2 s, kills the child process (SIGKILL), reboots, rejoins, asserts position continuity within 1 u. Mark the test as integration (runs in CI with a 60 s timeout).
Run full suite; confirm flush latency logged under 8 ms at p95 in the test output.

technicalNotes: 30 s flush granularity means a hard crash loses up to 30 s of position — acceptable per PRD (state continuity, not frame-exact).
Keep the flush transaction small: one UPDATE per ship, no WAL checkpoint inside.
